findings.finding: The plan says `test_pr_review_workflow_shape.py` only checks the env var name and that the new value will be “manually confirmed.” That leaves the exact `SHIPWRIGHT_PR_REVIEW_MODEL = deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` acceptance criterion unprotected against drift.
findings.suggestion: Extend the workflow-shape test to assert the env var value equals the new default model, or parse the workflow YAML and compare it to `DEFAULT_MODEL`.  6. Shared-library import path may be brittle in tests/local runs

findings.suggestion: Mirror the exact existing `external_review.py` wiring, prefer lazy import only on the DeepSeek branch if possible, and add a test that imports `pr_review_openrouter` without requiring live config or network access.

findings.finding: The plan loads `external_review.json` unconditionally after model resolution. This creates a new runtime dependency for every model, including an operator override to Sonnet or a future non-DeepSeek model. A missing, malformed, or otherwise unreadable external-review config would then break PR review even though no DeepSeek routing policy is needed. findings.finding: The proposed fail-closed handling catches `DeepSeekRoutingPolicyError`, but it is unclear whether `load_review_config()` can also raise distinct configuration, file, JSON-decode, or path-resolution exceptions before `resolve_extra_body()` is reached. findings.suggestion: Identify and catch the documented config-loader exception(s) as well as `DeepSeekRoutingPolicyError` within the DeepSeek-only branch. Ensure the protected block includes both config loading and routing-body construction, and add tests for malformed JSON/config-load failure in addition to a malformed `deepseek_routing` object.

findings.finding: The plan relies on the current working directory for `load_review_config()` (“this script always runs from the monorepo's own checkout root”). That assumption is fragile for direct script invocation, test runners, reusable workflows, and future CI refactors. It also introduces a new cross-tree import/path dependency from plugin code to `shared/scripts/lib`.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the repository root from the script/module location using the repository’s established root-discovery utility or the same robust mechanism used by other security scripts, then pass it explicitly to `load_review_config(project_root=...)` if supported. Import both `deepseek_openrouter_extra_body` and `DeepSeekRoutingPolicyError` through one canonical module path so the exception class being raised is guaranteed to be the one being caught.

findings.finding: The workflow verification is intentionally left as manual confirmation even though the acceptance criterion requires the workflow value to match `DEFAULT_MODEL`. The existing workflow test checks only that the environment-variable name exists, so it will not catch an accidental stale Sonnet value or later divergence.
findings.suggestion: Extend `test_pr_review_workflow_shape.py` to assert that `SHIPWRIGHT_PR_REVIEW_MODEL` is exactly `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`, ideally comparing it to the imported `DEFAULT_MODEL` where the test architecture permits. This makes the dual-source configuration requirement enforceable in CI.

findings.finding: The mini-plan is inconsistent about `extra_body`: it first proposes `dict | None = None`, then specifies a mutable `dict = {}` default. A mutable default is unnecessary and can cause state leakage if a future implementation mutates or normalizes the body. Separate tests of `resolve_extra_body()` and `_post_openrouter()` also do not fully prove that `main()` threads the resolved DeepSeek body into the actual call.
findings.suggestion: Use `extra_body: Mapping[str, object] | None = None` and merge with `if extra_body: payload.update(extra_body)`. Add a successful DeepSeek `main()` test that captures the arguments passed to `call_openrouter` and asserts the complete shared routing body, alongside the existing no-call failure test.  Overall, reusing the shared DeepSeek routing policy is the correct security-preserving approach, and the model-specific routing design is sound. The plan should be revised to avoid making non-DeepSeek operation depend on DeepSeek config and to make config/path failures reliably fail closed. SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

findings.finding: `_SHARED_LIB = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4] / "shared" / "scripts" / "lib"` is off by one: from `plugins/<plugin>/tests/` the repo root is `parents[3]`. `parents[4]` is the directory ABOVE the repo root, so the computed path does not exist and a bogus entry is inserted at sys.path[0] for the whole session. The import on the next line succeeds only by accident, because importing pr_review_model_policy already inserted the correct shared-lib path as a side effect.
findings.suggestion: Use `parents[3]`.

findings.finding: The central security invariant of this diff — that the DEFAULT (DeepSeek) model actually delivers the ZDR provider body through main() to call_openrouter — has no end-to-end assertion. Only the negative arm (non-DeepSeek override returns {}) is pinned.
findings.suggestion: Add a sibling test with the default model that runs main() through _wire and asserts the ZDR provider body reached call_openrouter.

findings.finding: except (DeepSeekRoutingPolicyError, OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) misses UnicodeDecodeError (non-UTF-8 config file) and AttributeError (a config that parses to a valid non-object). Both escape as an unredacted traceback exiting 1 instead of the documented redacted EXIT_ERROR.
findings.suggestion: Widen to except Exception, matching the two neighboring boundaries in main().

findings.finding: Both fail-closed tests assert only that call_openrouter was never invoked, not that fetch_pr_diff/read_reviewed_head were also unreached (the stricter ordering the AC requires).
findings.suggestion: Have _wire count fetch_pr_diff and read_reviewed_head invocations and assert both are 0 in the two fail-closed tests.

findings.finding: `if fn is post_review_state_fn:` distinguishes the two posting failures by object identity, which becomes unreliable now that the posters are caller-supplied (a caller passing the same callable for both would misattribute a comment-post failure to the state).
findings.suggestion: Carry the distinction explicitly in the loop tuple instead of identity comparison.

findings.finding: Because DEFAULT_MODEL is now a DeepSeek identity, every main() orchestration test in test_pr_review_script.py and test_pr_review_stale_verdicts.py transitively runs the REAL resolve_extra_body against the real shared/config/external_review.json — an implicit, undocumented coupling unrelated to what those suites test.
findings.suggestion: Stub resolve_extra_body to {} inside those _wire helpers so only the DeepSeek-specific modules own the config dependency.

code.disposition: all 6 findings fixed; see spec Code Review section

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: swapping the required PR-review gate's model to deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro is safe because a live probe confirmed the payload works and the operator accepted 'no additional rollback machinery' — allow_fallbacks:false + only=[novita,together], and together has no live endpoint for this model (this iterate's own documented known limitation) leaves exactly ONE provider serving a REQUIRED merge gate. A novita outage fails EVERY Tier-3 PR's required check simultaneously. Rollback is circular: SHIPWRIGHT_PR_REVIEW_MODEL is hardcoded in pr-review-run.yml, workflow_run always runs the DEFAULT BRANCH's copy of that workflow (never the PR's), so a rollback PR is reviewed by main's own still-broken logic and cannot go green through the normal path. Recovery = gh pr merge --admin. Nothing in the spec/workflow documented this.
findings.suggestion: Either engineer redundancy, or accept it explicitly and document the admin-override recovery procedure next to the model env var.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: reusing the cascade's ZDR routing config is purely additive — shared/config/external_review.json is now load-bearing for the required PR-review gate (a config-only drift reds every Tier-3 PR), but was not in review_record_tier.py's SENSITIVE_PATH_RE alongside the lib code it configures.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: the Goal's framing ('PR diffs are never sent through an unverified OpenRouter route') reads as a property of the gate generally — It's a property of the deepseek/ namespace only (AC-3's deliberate short-circuit) — a router/aggregator model identity outside that namespace gets no provider pin at all.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: the dependency-injected posters in post_verdict are safe now that the is_state flag replaced identity comparison — post_comment_fn/post_review_state_fn are bare Callable with different arities; a future mismatched call site raises TypeError inside the best-effort try, silently suppressing the stale-verdict cleanup.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: the broadened except Exception around resolve_extra_body() is harmless — It reports every exception as 'reviewer misconfigured (DeepSeek ZDR routing policy)' even when the real cause is a code bug, misdirecting on-call diagnosis. findings.suggestion: Include type(e).__name__ in the stderr line; comment why the except must stay broad.
